First, we remove the second row and second column: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075201/assets/09bd73c7e51abcad8efa354317519a2687601b3ccdbfea0ac2b6222f75b3397e.png)

Next, we calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}7x & -3y \\ -y & 5\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}7x & -3y \\ -y & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =7x\cdot 5-(-3y)\cdot (-y) \\  & =35x-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
For the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 3 \\ 5 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}].$
find the minor ${M}_{23}$ of the entry ${a}_{23}.$

${M}_{23}=${{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The minor of ${a}_{23}=-1$ (second row, third column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $-1$ are removed: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${a}_{23}=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{23} & =\text{det}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot 6-(-4)\cdot 0 \\  & =12-0 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
